paragraphs: On the anniversary of their grandmother's death, the Rahman family visits the cemetery {{mask_1}} she is buried. They follow a stone path {{mask_2}} winds between old trees. Their grandmother, {{mask_3}} had taught literature for many years, is remembered with affection. The family brings a small bouquet {{mask_4}} they arranged at home. They also carry a notebook, {{mask_5}} contains some of her favorite poems.

Aunt Samira tells the children about the woman {{mask_6}} encouraged her students to read widely. She recalls a story {{mask_7}} her grandmother used to tell after dinner. The family pauses beside a bench {{mask_8}} they can sit and talk quietly. Their uncle, {{mask_9}} lives in another city, has joined them for the visit. He brings flowers {{mask_10}} colors remind him of his grandmother's garden.

A caretaker {{mask_11}} the family recognizes from earlier visits greets them near the entrance. He points out a section {{mask_12}} recently planted trees provide shade. The family finds the grave {{mask_13}} is marked with a simple stone. They gently remove leaves {{mask_14}} have gathered around its base. The children place the flowers in a small jar {{mask_15}} their aunt has brought.

While they sit together, each person shares a memory {{mask_16}} reflects something their grandmother taught them. Samira describes the classroom {{mask_17}} her grandmother first began teaching. Her cousin, {{mask_18}} has brought a photograph from an old family album, passes it around. The picture, {{mask_19}} was taken during a summer gathering, makes everyone smile. Before leaving, they thank the caretaker {{mask_20}} keeps the cemetery paths clean and welcoming.
